A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Knowledgeable-R1. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching. Internal reporting inconsistencies do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations and component ablations in Tables 2–4, with additional model results in Appendix F.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and adds SFT comparisons, sensitivity experiments, training-dynamics observations and context-dependence diagnostics.

M1.justification: The PK/CK/RPK objectives, adaptive modulation, default weights and inference procedure remain unchanged. Section 3.2 clarifies that RPK reuses PK trajectories, already encoded in v2's algorithm. The appendix equation correction aligns the pseudocode with the existing main-text objective rather than establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: The datasets and five main scenario families are retained. Appendix F adds controlled ConFiQA test conditions with 1, 2, 4 or 8 misleading passages, extending adversarial input conditions. ExplainCPE becoming ExplainPE is a naming correction, not a new medical dataset.

E2.justification: v4 adds a supervised fine-tuning baseline using the same context mixture and explicit conflict-handling instructions, evaluated in Table 2 and the new Table 13 analysis. Existing comparators remain. CK-PLUG was already evaluated in v2 Tables 2–3 and Appendix A despite its omission from the earlier main-text baseline list.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs sweep fixed beta values, advantage and objective weights, and good/bad training-context ratios; compare trained models with and without context; and introduce factuality and KL diagnostics. Existing splits, model coverage and default training settings remain. The retrieval and rollout clarifications do not establish changes to the original experiments.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component-removal ablations, Section 4.3 and Appendices A–G investigate beta dynamics and sensitivity, weighting robustness, the correct/adversarial-context trade-off, training-noise dependence, misleading-passage counts and context reliance. New stratification by RAG-prompting correctness also examines whether gains extend to previously failed examples.

E5.justification: Appendix J newly reports stability across 200+ training runs covering GRPO and Knowledgeable-R1 configurations. This adds aggregate run-count information without establishing increased repetitions per setting. Neither version reports per-setting seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing numerical entries in Tables 2–4 and v2 Table 5, now v4 Table 14, are unchanged. Substantial additions include SFT scores and the new diagnostic and sensitivity results. For example, Table 10 reports adversarial accuracy of 17.34% versus GRPO's 14.31% under 99:1 good/bad training contexts. These are newly reported conditions, not across-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects the unclipped RPK objective term from the PK advantage A_i to the transformed RPK advantage T(Â_i), resolving its inconsistency with Section 3.5. Other mathematical changes are notation or equation numbering; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contribution and claims remain joint PK/CK learning with asymmetric modulation for resistance to contextual interference while preserving useful context use. Changing the headline gain from 23% to approximately 22.9% and adding a Table 3 pointer refine reporting without materially changing the claim's scope.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly discusses the S1/S2 performance trade-off and motivates the default weights as prioritizing adversarial robustness. It newly interprets noise-ratio robustness and context diagnostics as learned knowledge arbitration, and beta convergence as rapid calibration. These substantially expand the mechanism discussion, sometimes using stronger causal language than the evidence establishes. The limitations paragraph is retained.

D1.justification: New disclosures explain RPK trajectory reuse, dataset-provided context ordering and truncation, matched rollout allocation, shared forward passes and the SFT prompt. Appendix J adds epoch times of 1h38m versus GRPO's 1h19m. Existing core hyperparameters, hardware and code-access statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the substantive positioning relative to prior research are retained. The added Nature reference is the publication version of the already cited DeepSeek-R1 work. Expanded baseline descriptions do not introduce a distinct prior-work relationship or novelty claim.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative remain intact. v4 adds targeted method and setup explanations, condenses the ablation discussion, rewrites the conclusion and standardizes some terminology. New analysis sections precede the original appendices, which are retained as H–N.

P2.justification: v4 adds nine analysis tables, Tables 5–13, SFT rows in Table 2 and an SFT prompt box. Existing tables and prompt displays are redistributed, including the additional-model table becoming Table 14. Figure 1's graphic and inset chart already existed; its caption is expanded.

improvement.justification: The SFT comparison, controlled weighting/noise analyses, RPK clarification and Algorithm 1 correction improve empirical support and reproducibility. However, new Tables 9 and 11 use MC labels alongside reference values matching MR results, and several mechanistic conclusions overstate what the diagnostics establish. The useful additions therefore support a limited overall quality gain.
